_comment: LEAN SeisBench dtype matrix: GPU-first, smaller sweeps, ~O(10^5) rows vs 10^6+ for full grid. FP32 full-precision reference is baseline_annotate only (no lean_pytorch fp32). Lean sweep: FP16/BF16, plus torch.compile variants restricted to PhaseNet models via model_labels. EQT FP16 lean without compile is still skipped in the driver. For full sweeps see seisbench_dtype_matrix_full.json.
_comment_devices: Single GPU (cuda:0) avoids duplicating the whole grid on cuda:1. Add "cuda:1" if you need per-device deltas. CPU omitted here—add "cpu" plus cpu_backends_override (short list) if you need CPU reference numbers without 6× compile cost.
_comment_n_samples: P-centered raw window length at model sampling rate (6000 ≈ 3000 samples before P when unclipped).
_comment_dual_gpu_serial: Misleading legacy name: this flag does NOT run GPUs sequentially. It only adds an extra unpinned-CPU trial whose label happens to be 'lean_pytorch_dual_serial'. The actual dual-GPU runner always runs both devices concurrently (threaded variant: max(shard0, shard1) wall time; process variant: same). Leave false to avoid duplicate-trial confusion.
_comment_dual_gpu_use_process_runner_for: When true and a backend has compile=true, dual-GPU work routes through rapid.runners.dual_gpu_process (separate Python interpreters + CUDA contexts via torch.multiprocessing) instead of being driver-skipped. This is the only safe configuration for torch.compile across two GPUs: each worker process owns its own Inductor and CUDA-graph state, so there is no cross-thread context corruption. Lean dual-GPU cells without compile keep using the threaded runner.
_comment_cpus: CPU-affinity sweep applied to the dual-GPU driver process. Ignored unless dual_gpu is true.
_comment_cpu_reference: Example CPU spot-check: "devices": ["cpu", "cuda:0"], "cpu_backends_override": [{"name":"lean_pytorch","dtype":"fp16"},{"name":"lean_pytorch","dtype":"bf16"}] (FP32 via baseline_annotate on CPU when include_baseline is true).
